answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to a personal orchard of sequential memory-hard proofs. Every epoch the agent must advance its private state by a fixed delta of work that cannot be precomputed or shared. An attacker who spins up many clones must fund a separate canyon of dedicated sequential RAM and CPU cycles for each one; the total cost grows linearly with the number of fakes and cannot be amortized, pricing the attack out of the reward pool.
